title: Choose the visual world for ENF
question: The roll assigned the Signal Box Panel. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Signal Box Panel
options.lineage: JR / British Rail route-setting (NX) panels in signal cabins
options.thesis: The fleet as a live track diagram: every doorway is a route that is set or cancelled with one button.
options.viewport: The whole screen is the panel: doorway signals on the left, one trunk into the fleet junction, agent platforms on the right, route lamps lit by verdict, cancel buttons sitting on the diagram itself.
options.risk: If lamps and plates are drawn timidly it reads as a flat diagram; it needs real panel material to land from 3 m.

raised.raise: Dead routes stay drawn as unlit ghost lamps; absence is designed, never removed.
Every doorway and agent carries one stencilled panel code (D1-D4, A1-A3) shared by diagram, grid and log.
One button press visibly propagates along every linked segment, in track order.

options.label: Tokyo Line Map
options.lineage: JR and Tokyo Metro line diagrams with numbered stations
options.thesis: The fleet is one line; every merchant doorway is a station on it, numbered like JY01.
options.viewport: A horizontal line map across the top half with stations as doorways and branches as agents; service suspended shows as a greyed line segment.
options.risk: Transit maps are a familiar move for anything network-shaped; strong locally in Tokyo but easy to guess.

options.label: Seven-Segment Scoreboard
options.thesis: Every count and verdict as lit segments that read from the back of the hall.
options.viewport: A scoreboard wall of doorway x agent cells, each a lit segment word, with the block number as a big digit totem.
options.case: Holds product clarity at distance for numbers, but loses audience identification and cannot draw the one-fleet topology.
options.risk: Drifts toward the dark-neon crypto look you ruled out.

options.label: Convention Circle Catalog
options.lineage: Comiket circle catalogs and hall maps
options.thesis: Doorways as table codes in a packed catalog grid keyed to a hall map.
options.viewport: A numbered grid of doorway cells with a folded hall map.
options.case: Judges do not read an agent fleet as a hall of tables; the fleet topology gets lost.
options.kept: Codes that link a grid cell to its place on the map.

options.label: Miura-Fold Sheet
options.thesis: One pull deploys the whole crease field.
options.viewport: A folded sheet that unfolds into doorways.
options.case: The propagation idea fits, the paper metaphor does not; clarity drops.
options.risk: Reads as art piece, not tool.
options.kept: One action propagating across linked parts.

options.label: ASCII Live Render
options.thesis: The topology as a live glyph field.
options.viewport: A character-grid rendering of the fleet.
options.case: Illegible from 3 m and lands in the hacker-green rut.
options.kept: One strict grid ruling the whole face.

options.label: Parametric Identity
options.thesis: A mark that reseeds the whole UI.
options.viewport: An animated mark with seeded panels.
options.case: Decoration without the mechanism; judges learn nothing.
options.kept: One source drives every color: the verdict lamp set is the only color system.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Cutting weather blocks into temporary buildings.
options.case: No path from the metaphor to namespaces.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean web3 dashboard in the Etherscan and ENS-app family, done with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Stats row, graph panel, verdict grid and inspector in a clean light layout.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other hackathon dashboard by design.
